judge_comment: Directly targets the manual quote-comparison pain point via document extraction, doesn't overlap with the claims-summary assistant, and minimal AI Act risk with 30% time saved is plausible for a structured extraction task.

This use case directly targets the rushed-deadline and complexity pain points by synthesizing claims history and risk factors into a discussion agenda, is distinct from the document extraction tool (analysis vs. extraction), and minimal AI Act risk with indirect GDPR is defensible for an internal analytical/summarization assistant.

Directly targets the inconsistent-decision and multi-system-check pain points with a plausible time saving, is distinct from the pure information-retrieval assistant (this one makes a recommendation), and since it's not a recruitment/worker-evaluation/credit-scoring type use case, "minimal" risk under the EU AI Act is correct though GDPR impact from condition photos/personal data could arguably be "direct" rather than "indirect".

This use case addresses the multi-system lookup pain point well and is correctly rated minimal risk since it only aggregates information without deciding, but it substantially overlaps the classifier use case which already surfaces the same order/condition/policy data as part of its recommendation.

Directly targets the manual extraction/standardization bottleneck and is distinct from the downstream matching/classification use case; minimal AI Act risk and 35% time savings are plausible for a well-scoped extraction task, though bank statements plus GL data could carry some personal data so indirect GDPR is reasonable.

Directly targets the core matching/discrepancy-tracing pain point, is distinct from the upstream extraction use case, and minimal AI Act risk plus 30% time savings are plausible for a well-scoped matching classifier.

Directly targets the core copy-paste/formatting pain point with a plausible time-saving estimate, does not overlap with the separate approval-tracking classifier, and content drafting for social posts is correctly rated minimal risk under the AI Act.

Directly targets the approval-tracking pain point without overlapping the content-drafting use case, with a conservative time-saved estimate and correctly minimal AI Act risk since this is internal workflow status tracking, not worker evaluation.

Directly targets the stated severity inconsistency pain point with a distinct classification step that doesn't overlap the dedup or routing use cases; minimal AI Act risk is appropriate since IT ticket triage isn't an Annex III category, and the 25% time saving is plausible for a simple classification task.

Directly addresses the duplicate-detection pain point without overlapping the classification or assignment use cases; minimal AI Act risk is correct since this is operational IT deduplication, not an Annex III category, though "document_extraction" is a slight mislabel for what is really a similarity/matching task.

This directly targets the ownership-assignment pain point and doesn't overlap the classification/dedup use cases, but assigning work based on an engineer's past performance/behavior and workload falls under Annex III task-allocation/worker-evaluation and should be labeled high-risk, not minimal.

Directly targets the exception-handling pain point with a distinct classification step from the extraction use case; 35% time saved is plausible and minimal risk is correct since this is not worker performance evaluation but transaction classification.

Addresses a real pre-processing pain point distinct from the classification use case, with plausible time savings and correctly minimal AI Act risk since commission calculation is not an Annex III category.

This directly tackles the disconnected-channels and manual-checking pain points with a plausible time saving, and is complementary (not overlapping) with the downstream classification use case; however, since this extraction feeds directly into right-to-work verification and onboarding decisions tied to employment eligibility, it arguably falls under the recruitment/employment Annex III category and should be flagged as high-risk rather than minimal.

This directly addresses the compliance-checking pain point and complements the extraction use case without duplicating it, but classifying employment eligibility/right-to-work status for onboarding is closely tied to employment decisions and should arguably be scrutinized as higher risk given GDPR-sensitive data and employment consequences, though it doesn't squarely fall under Annex III recruitment/evaluation categories so 'minimal' is defensible but borderline; pct_time_saved of 30% seems reasonable for a 20-minute task.

Directly targets the inconsistent free-text notes pain point via structured extraction, is distinct from the downstream classification/tracking use cases, and minimal risk is correctly assigned since this is not an Annex III category (though pct_time_saved of 35% is plausible but slightly optimistic for extraction alone).

Directly addresses the recurring-hazard cross-referencing pain point with a defensible time-saving estimate, correctly rated minimal risk since it's a safety pattern classifier not covered by Annex III, though it has moderate conceptual overlap with the corrective-action matching assistant.

Directly targets the corrective-action tracking pain point without duplicating the extraction or classification use cases; minimal AI Act risk is reasonable since this is an internal safety-logistics tool, though pct_time_saved of 15% seems conservative but defensible.
